name: GPS Spoofing — Highway Position Offset
description:
## GPS Spoofing — Highway Position Offset

Evaluates receiver behaviour when a **GNSS spoofer** introduces a 500 m position offset (NE direction) during a highway drive.

The spoofer targets GPS L1 C/A on the most visible PRNs, transmitting counterfeit signals with a synthesised position offset of approximately 354 m East and 354 m North (~500 m total displacement).

**Route:** Dual-carriageway access road, approx. 6 km straight section.

**Expected outcome:** The receiver's reported position drifts up to 500 m from the ground-truth track. The GT system records the true position throughout, enabling post-run KPI analysis.

steps.driver_instructions:
Enter the highway and accelerate to the **test speed of 90 km/h**. Maintain steady speed in the right lane.

Confirm that both the VDL and GT systems are publishing data. The RSG is armed but not yet transmitting.

The RSG activates the GPS spoofer targeting PRNs 1, 3, 6, 11, 17, 22 at −10 dBm. A **500 m NE position offset** is introduced gradually.

Maintain 90 km/h. The receiver's displayed position will begin to diverge from the true vehicle position. Do not adjust speed or lane.

The spoofer continues transmitting with the full 500 m offset active. **Maintain 90 km/h** and continue driving straight.

Note any receiver integrity flags (NMEA `GBS` or `GRS` sentences). The GT track and VDL track divergence should be clearly visible in Grafana.

The RSG disables the spoofer. **Reduce speed to 30 km/h** and prepare to exit the highway at the next junction.

Monitor the receiver for re-convergence with the true position. Record the time taken for the reported position to return within 10 m of the GT reference.
